ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence for all foreign and domestic politically exposed persons under sections 23-25 of the AML/CFT Act 2009; mandatory screening against UN Security Council Consolidated Lists, OFAC SDN List (best practice for cross-border litigation), UK OFSI Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, Interpol notices, and New Zealand domestic sanctions lists (Russia Sanctions Act 2022 and autonomous sanctions frameworks); ongoing transaction monitoring, annual refresh for UBOs and PEPs, and five-year record retention under the AML/CFT Act.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office (www.companiesoffice.govt.nz) — online Companies Register and Name Reservation Service (COMP)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Latin script and English language, with permissible Maori macrons; non-English names must be transliterated into romanized form; the Registrar may reject names that are misleading as to nature, falsely suggest Crown or government connection, or are not clearly distinguishable from existing registered names; punctuation and special characters are limited.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The initial name reservation is valid for 20 working days. A written request to the Registrar of Companies can extend the reservation once for a further 20 working days. If the Registrar refuses a name, the applicant receives a written notice stating the statutory grounds of refusal; the applicant may file a reconsideration request within 20 working days, submitting evidence of distinctiveness and consent from any affected regulator or body. If the refusal is maintained, an appeal may be lodged with the High Court of New Zealand under section 25 of the Companies Act 1993, including judicial review under the Senior Courts Act 2016. Legal counsel must file the appeal within 30 calendar days of the final refusal; injunctive relief is available where the refusal causes imminent commercial prejudice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only as a professional registered office located at a physical New Zealand street address (e.g., the premises of a registered corporate service provider or a law firm). A pure virtual mailbox or post-office box does not satisfy section 18 of the Companies Act 1993. The International Company must maintain a registered agent resident in New Zealand capable of receiving legal process on behalf of the litigation chambers; for the IOLTA trust account, a physical NZ presence or locally admitted principal is required for NZ banking and AML/CFT compliance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low_Risk_Standard sector: estimated under 10% probability per annum of an unannounced physical on-site inspection by the Department of Internal Affairs (AML/CFT Supervisor) during the first operating year. However, the DIA and the New Zealand Law Society conduct periodic 'mystery shopper' and compliance inspections, and a biennial audit cycle is standard. If the client profile includes high-net-worth foreign PEPs or sanctions-sensitive cross-border litigation, the inspection probability increases to a medium range (approximately 15-25% per annum), particularly where trust accounts and wire rails are involved.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), ss 6, 10, 12-16, 18-25, 37, 51-52, 118, 120, 128, 130, 151-159, 189-201, 386; Companies (Fees) Regulations 1998; additionally governed for legal-service purposes by the Lawyers and Conveyancers Act 2006, ss 6, 10, and the Lawyers and Conveyancers Act 2006 (Incorporated Law Firms) Regulations 2008; Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office (Ngā Kaporeihana), Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), 15 Stout Street, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form NZCN1 — Application for Incorporation of a Company (including the prescribed particulars of directors, shareholders, registered office, and address for service) together with the company constitution or a statement adopting the default constitution in Schedule 1 of the Companies Act 1993
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement apply under the Companies Act 1993; shares may be issued without nominal or paid-up value and the company may incorporate on nil or nominal capitalization (e.g., 100 ordinary shares of NZ$1.00 each). The directors must execute a solvency certificate under s 52 of the Companies Act 1993 for any share issue, and the share capital account must be maintained as a stated capital account under s 51.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF CK_IC (NEW ZEALAND INTERNATIONAL COMPANY): RESOLVED, that the subscribers subscribe to the share capital set out in Schedule A (100 ordinary shares of NZ$1.00 each no par value), and that the directors be and are authorised to issue any nil-paid or partly-paid shares in accordance with s 37(4) of the Companies Act 1993, with the solvency certificate under s 52 executed by each director. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Company be and is hereby established at Level 6, 45 Queen Street, Auckland 1010, New Zealand, as registered with the Registrar of Companies pursuant to s 189 of the Companies Act 1993. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name A] be appointed Managing Director, [Name B] be appointed Finance Director, and [Name C] be appointed Company Secretary, each to hold office for a term of three years pursuant to s 153, and that all necessary consents under s 151 be filed with the Companies Office. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the directors be and are authorised to execute and file the application to the New Zealand Law Society for approval as an incorporated law firm and to open the IOLTA-compliant client trust account, the general operating account, and the designated AML/CFT compliance account at an authorised New Zealand bank, and that the AML/CFT compliance officer be appointed within five business days under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Company constitution tabled at this meeting be and is hereby adopted and registered as the constitution of the Company effective as of registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Companies Register), Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an online search of the New Zealand Companies Register to confirm that the proposed name 'CK International Company NZ Limited' is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing, reserved, or incorporated name under ss 20-22 of the Companies Act 1993. Names that are offensive, imply Crown patronage, or suggest a restricted or regulated activity without lawful authority must be avoided under ss 23-24. Optionally file an online name reservation to hold the preferred name for 20 working days; a reservation materially reduces the risk of rejection at the incorporation stage.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name memorandum
Certified name availability search report from the NZ Companies Register
Identity document of the applicant (passport or national identity card)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a name rejection notice, refile a fresh search and incorporation application using a structurally and phonetically distinct name, or make written representations to the Registrar. A formal appeal against refusal on prohibited grounds lies to the High Court of New Zealand under s 25 of the Companies Act 1993.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Constitution and Statutory Incorporation Application (NZCN1)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company founders and counsel, with submission through the New Zealand Companies Office online electronic filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the company constitution under s 18 of the Companies Act 1993 or adopt the default constitution in Schedule 1. Complete Form NZCN1 (Application for Incorporation of a Company) capturing the company name, registered office address, address for service, full legal names, dates and places of birth, former names, and residential or business addresses of each director, the share structure, and the shareholder allotment. Attach the constitution and verify compliance with s 19 content requirements. For an incorporated law firm, include a purpose clause for 'cross-border commercial litigation, arbitration, and dispute resolution services' as contemplated by the Lawyers and Conveyancers Act 2006 and the Incorporated Law Firms Regulations 2008.
required_dossiers: Form NZCN1 (Incorporation Application)
Company constitution or Schedule 1 default adoption statement
Signed consents of directors (s 151 Companies Act 1993)
Shareholder/subscriber consent forms
AML/CFT identity verification documents for all beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the Companies Office returns an incomplete or non-compliant application, the applicant will be advised and may cure defects within 15 working days through the online portal. If the constitution is deficient, amend and refile the constitution together with a solicitor's certificate of compliance, or adopt the statutory default constitution to remove the objection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inaugural Board Meeting and Officer Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of CK_IC (acting under section 118 of the Companies Act 1993)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the inaugural board meeting with all duly notified directors present. Pass the first board resolution to subscribe for shares, adopt the registered office, appoint the Managing Director, Finance Director, Company Secretary, and the AML/CFT compliance officer. Ensure at least one director is a natural person resident in New Zealand or an enforcement country (e.g., Australia) as required by s 152 of the Companies Act 1993, and that no director acts without the signed consent required by s 151. Record the proceedings in the company minute book and open the statutory registers.
required_dossiers: Notice of meeting and agenda
Directors' declarations of consent and certificate of compliance (ss 151 and 159 Companies Act 1993)
First board resolution document
Register of directors and register of shareholders opening entries
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any procedural defect in board action may be cured by a ratification resolution under s 180 of the Companies Act 1993 (validation of defective acts). If a director's written consent is missing, obtain a signed consent nunc pro tunc and file the correction notice; the Registrar may also issue a certificate of correction under s 177.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Government Filing, Statutory Fee Payment, and Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office (MBIE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed Form NZCN1 and all accompanying constitution and consent documents through the New Zealand Companies Office online register (www.companiesoffice.govt.nz). Pay the prescribed incorporation fee (NZD 105.40, approximate USD 65) by approved electronic payment. Upon satisfaction that all requirements in ss 13-14 of the Companies Act 1993 are met, the Registrar enters the company into the Companies Register and issues the Certificate of Incorporation under s 12. The certificate is conclusive evidence of incorporation, and the company's separate legal personality commences on the date and time stated therein.
required_dossiers: Completed and certified Form NZCN1
Constitution PDF in the exact company name
Digital payment receipt confirming the filing fee
Electronic signatures of all subscribers and directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar declines incorporation, the applicant may make written reps, remedy identified deficiencies and resubmit through the portal; a disputed refusal can be appealed to the High Court of New Zealand by way of judicial review. If the Registrar accepts the application but issues a post-filing query, the applicant has a 15-day statutory cure period to respond with amended particulars.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Governance Establishment and Register Onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of CK_IC, New Zealand Companies Office, and New Zealand Law Society (where legal services are provided)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within ten business days of the Certificate of Incorporation, open the statutory registers (shareholder register, director register, charge register, and register of interests) at the registered office. Issue share certificates and file the share allotment return with the Companies Office. Appoint the AML/CFT compliance officer and approve the written AML/CFT compliance programme under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009. For legal services, submit the application to the New Zealand Law Society for approval as an incorporated law firm, and open the IOLTA-compliant client trust account at an authorised New Zealand bank with written trust account mandate and audit designation.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Company extract from the Companies Register
Share certificates and share allotment return
AML/CFT compliance programme and business risk assessment
New Zealand Law Society incorporated law firm application form
Bank trust account mandate and signatory resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Omitted or late filings may be cured by immediate electronic submission to the Companies Register and an application to waive or remit late-filing penalties under Regulation 7 of the Companies (Fees) Regulations 1998. If the New Zealand Law Society refuses incorporated-law-firm approval, appeal to the Legal Complaints Review Officer and reconstitute the ownership and directorship structure to meet the 100% lawyer-ownership and control requirements under s 6 of the Lawyers and Conveyancers Act 2006.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: New Zealand Law Society Te Kāhui Ture o Aotearoa (NZLS) — Regulatory Board for Legal Services; Legal Complaints Review Officer; Financial Markets Authority (FMA) for AML/CFT supervision; and the Auckland Council or relevant territorial authority for physical business premises licensing
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Certificate of Approval as an Incorporated Law Firm under s 6 of the Lawyers and Conveyancers Act 2006 and the Lawyers and Conveyancers Act 2006 (Incorporated Law Firms) Regulations 2008, together with individual New Zealand Law Society Practising Certificates for each director-lawyer providing cross-border commercial litigation, arbitration, and asset tracing services

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) of New Zealand, in coordination with the relevant regional council and territorial authority under the Resource Management Act 1991 and the Resource Management (Assessment of Environmental Effects) Regulations 1999
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Registration Tier — Category 2 (Permitted Commercial Office Use): no full environmental impact assessment or EIA report is required for office-based litigation chambers; a low-risk activity registration and, where the building use changes materially, a resource consent under ss 127-127A of the Resource Management Act 1991 may be required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the Resource Management (National Environmental Standards for Air Quality) Regulations 2004 for volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions, with indoor total VOC concentration not exceeding 500 ppb in office fit-out materials; trade-waste discharge compliance with the local council Trade Waste Bylaw (pH 6-10, total suspended solids < 600 mg/L, biochemical oxygen demand < 600 mg/L, fats/oils < 100 mg/L); hazardous waste segregation and certified destruction of confidential client records in accordance with the Waste Management (Disposal and Recovery) provisions and the Privacy Act 2020.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate under the Fire and Emergency New Zealand (Fire Safety, Fire and Emergency Evacuation Procedures) Regulations 2018; Building Warrant of Fitness and annual structural load inspection certificate under ss 115-120 of the Building Act 2004; Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 workplace clearance and the Health and Safety at Work (General Risk and Workplace Management) Regulations 2016; emergency evacuation procedure manual; and electrical installation compliance certificate under the Electricity (Safety) Regulations 2010.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department ('Te Tari Taake'), Government of New Zealand — national tax administration and collection body; digital service channel: myIR Secure Online Services (https://www.ird.govt.nz); corporate registry interface: New Zealand Companies Office and the New Zealand Business Number register (https://www.nzbn.govt.nz); chief executive officer: Commissioner of Inland Revenue.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 — Confirm non-resident status: an International Company incorporated outside New Zealand and not centrally managed and controlled in New Zealand is a non-resident company for income tax purposes under sections YD 2 and YD 4 of the Income Tax Act 2007. Step 2 — Appoint a New Zealand resident agent for service of notices unless an exemption applies, and file Form IRD 596 (Request for an IRD number - non-individual) with the Inland Revenue Department, accompanied by the certificate of incorporation, extract from the offshore register, constitutional documents, director and ultimate beneficial owner particulars, a certificate of tax residency issued by the home jurisdiction, and, for this regulated sector, evidence of New Zealand Law Society practising certificates and trust account authorisation. Step 3 — Obtain a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) through the Companies Office where the entity registers as an overseas company or establishes a branch; the NZBN is then linked to the IRD number. Step 4 — Register for GST under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 where taxable supplies in New Zealand exceed NZD 60,000 in a 12-month period, or where voluntary registration is sought to support zero-rating of exported legal services; the IRD number serves as the GST registration number, with no separate GST identifier. Step 5 — For non-resident suppliers of remote services to New Zealand residents, use the simplified non-resident supplier GST registration gateway available in myIR. Step 6 — Maintain statutory records under section 21 of the Tax Administration Act 1994 and section 75 of the GST Act 1985, and keep a current New Zealand address for service where required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — the CK International Company, being non-resident under the Income Tax Act 2007 and operating under an exempt offshore charter, is excluded from New Zealand entity-level income taxation in respect of all offshore-sourced commercial litigation revenues; New Zealand income tax applies only to income derived from sources in New Zealand under the territorial rules of sections YD 4 and YD 4B, and no look-through or flow-through election is deemed to apply. The entity is not a tax resident of New Zealand and has no New Zealand permanent establishment in respect of its cross-border litigation chambers activity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand self-assessment law does not contain a 'check-the-box' classification election. Elective mechanisms available to this taxpayer: (a) Look-Through Company (LTC) election under subpart HB of the Income Tax Act 2007 — available only to companies with qualifying New Zealand-resident shareholders and therefore not available without restructuring of this offshore IC; (b) grandfathered Qualifying Company (QC) election — closed to newly incorporated entities; (c) hybrid and branch mismatch elections under subpart FH (Taxation (Neutralising Base Erosion and Profit Shifting) Act 2018), including a compensating adjustment election where the IC is treated as fiscally transparent in the counterparty jurisdiction; (d) GST zero-rating election for exported services and remote services under section 11A(1)(k), (l) and (m) of the GST Act 1985; (e) option to voluntarily register for GST below the NZD 60,000 threshold in order to claim input tax credits and issue zero-rated invoices.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) — a comprehensive value-added tax imposed under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 and administered by the Inland Revenue Department; broad-based, destination-principle, credit-invoice VAT model with no sub-national sales tax component.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies made in New Zealand in any 12-month period (section 51 GST Act 1985); a separate compulsory registration threshold of NZD 60,000 per annum applies to non-resident suppliers of remote services supplied to New Zealand residents (sections 8B and 60 GST Act 1985); voluntary registration permitted below the threshold; once registered, the supplier must remain registered for a minimum of two years unless registration is cancelled by the Commissioner.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or transactional invoice validation regime. The Government has mandated Peppol-compliant e-invoicing for central government agencies on the buy-side since 17 March 2022; private-sector suppliers may voluntarily adopt e-invoicing through certified Peppol service providers using the four-corner interoperability model. GST tax invoices issued under section 24 of the GST Act 1985 may be created, transmitted, and retained electronically, but must contain the prescribed particulars including the supplier's name and registration number, date of issue, description and quantity of the supply, consideration, and the amount of GST or a statement of zero-rating; there is no Inland Revenue API pre-clearance or unique invoice authorisation code, and record-keeping must enable the Commissioner to verify output tax and zero-rating claims on audit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating at 0% GST applies: (1) to goods physically exported from New Zealand within 28 days of the time of supply (section 11(1)(a) GST Act 1985); (2) to services supplied to a non-resident who is outside New Zealand when the services are performed, unless supplied directly in connection with land in New Zealand or moveable personal property situated in New Zealand at the time of supply (section 11A(1)(k)); (3) to remote services supplied to a non-resident while the recipient is in New Zealand (section 11A(1)(l)); and (4) to services supplied in connection with moveable personal property situated outside New Zealand (section 11A(1)(m)). Cross-border commercial litigation services — arbitration advocacy, offshore court appearances, legal research, asset tracing, expert testimony, and document review — supplied to an offshore client qualify for zero-rating where the recipient is a non-resident, the services are not connected to New Zealand land or New Zealand moveable property, and the supplier holds contemporaneous evidence of the offshore nexus; the supplier must be GST-registered and may recover input tax attributable to the zero-rated supplies through the ordinary refund mechanism.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (Trade Single Window entry with New Zealand Customs Service clearance status and unique consignment reference) — applicable where physical exhibits or evidence items are exported as part of the litigation engagement and subject to the 28-day export rule
Bill of Lading, Sea Waybill, or Air Waybill evidencing physical export of goods from New Zealand to the foreign destination
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank foreign-currency receipt advice (SWIFT MT103) evidencing receipt of consideration from the offshore client account
Executed litigation engagement letter and fee agreement demonstrating the non-resident status of the recipient and the offshore situs of performance

Certificate of non-resident status or equivalent identification documentation (passport extract, corporate register extract, or beneficial ownership declaration) for the ultimate client, including trusts and corporate vehicles
Itemised GST tax invoice issued under section 24 GST Act 1985 showing zero-rated supplies and citing the statutory basis under section 11A(1)(k), (l), or (m)

Detailed schedule of services performed outside New Zealand, including arbitration venues, hearing dates, travel records, and confirmation that no supply was made in connection with New Zealand land or New Zealand moveable personal property
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: For the avoidance of doubt, New Zealand law does not prescribe a statutory foreign-currency repatriation window; the 180-day period stated above is applied as the contractual and evidentiary benchmark for confirming receipt of export consideration in zero-rating audits. Inland Revenue audits zero-rated export claims under the record-keeping and anti-avoidance provisions of the Tax Administration Act 1994 and the GST Act 1985. Where the zero-rating condition fails or the export documentation is deficient, the supply is re-characterised as a taxable supply at 15% GST, output tax becomes due from the time of supply, use-of-money interest runs under section 120 TAA 1994, and input credits are retrospectively clawed back. Civil shortfall penalties escalate by culpability: 20% for failure to take reasonable care, 20% for an unacceptable tax position, 40% for gross carelessness, 100% for an abusive tax position, and 150% for evasion or an arrangement intended to defeat the tax laws (section 141 TAA 1994). Late payment penalties accrue at 1% on day 8 and 4% on day 15 after the due date, followed by 1% per month (section 139A TAA 1994). Criminal prosecution under section 143A TAA 1994 for evasion or similar offences carries penalties of fines up to NZD 50,000 for an individual and NZD 250,000 for a body corporate, and imprisonment up to five years; absolute-liability offences under section 143B carry fines up to NZD 25,000 for an individual and NZD 100,000 for a company. Fraudulent export zero-rating schemes further expose the entity and its directors to disqualification proceedings, referral to the New Zealand Law Society under the Lawyers and Conveyancers Act 2006, and loss of practising certificates, in addition to the full monetary clawback and penalty exposure.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua) is the central bank and prudential supervisor of registered banks, operating the high-value payment and settlement system (ESAS). The Financial Markets Authority (FMA) is the conduct and market regulator under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013. The Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) of the New Zealand Police supervises suspicious transaction reporting and AML/CFT intelligence. New Zealand abolished dedicated exchange-control legislation in 1984 with the repeal of the Exchange Control Act 1953; foreign exchange is liberalised, the NZD is fully floating, and the Reserve Bank intervenes only in systemic-stress or financial-stability scenarios.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility under the IMF Article VIII framework. There are no surrender, approval, repatriation, or licensing requirements for inward investment, operating profits, professional fees, litigation settlement proceeds, or shareholder distributions of an International Company. The Overseas Investment Act 2005 applies only to the acquisition of sensitive land or significant business assets above prescribed thresholds, neither of which is engaged by a commercial litigation chambers conducting ISIC 6910 multi-jurisdictional arbitration and asset tracing. Profit remittance hurdles are nil; funds held in an IOLTA trust account or operational account may be converted freely at licensed dealing banks, and there is no differential treatment for non-resident shareholders.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. New Zealand imposes no statutory timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or surrender obligation for export receipts or export of services, including cross-border legal and arbitration services. Exporters and legal service providers may retain receipts in any convertible currency, hold net open FX positions within bank prudential limits, or convert at any licensed dealer without Reserve Bank approval. The only incidental obligation is statistical: financial institutions report balance-of-payments transactions to Statistics New Zealand for settlements typically at or above NZD 50,000, but this does not restrict the exporter and requires no central-bank filing by the International Company.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM as an ancillary FX and cross-border payment gateway; LOW as the primary trust or escrow clearing bank. New Zealand does not operate a bespoke electronic money institution licence category. A digital EMI or money-transfer provider must register on the Financial Service Providers Register (FSPR) under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008 and become a reporting entity under the AML/CFT Act 2009 with an approved AML/CFT programme. Offshore EMIs cannot directly access the Reserve Bank's ESAS settlement system or the domestic ACH clearing infrastructure, so same-day NZD trust disbursements require a sponsorship arrangement with a licensed registered bank. For IOLTA-grade client money, an unlicensed offshore EMI is legally constrained from acting as core custodian because professional trust funds must be held with an authorised deposit-taker under the Lawyers and Conveyancers Act 2006 where the chamber operates as a licensed practice.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors of a non-resident International Company are not statutorily required to appear physically in New Zealand. Section 14 of the AML/CFT Act 2009 requires that the identity of the customer and beneficial owners be verified from a reliable, independent source. In practice, the Tier 1 banks adopt a hybrid approach: remote onboarding is available to Low_Risk_Standard corporate clients with clean beneficial ownership, conditioned on a live video KYC interview of at least one director and all signatories, plus notarised or apostilled corporate record extracts and dual-source address verification. No in-branch attendance is generally required where principals reside in a recognised FATF/EAG jurisdiction. Where beneficial ownership is layered through a trust or offshore structure, banks may condition onboarding on a physical meeting at a foreign correspondent bank or at an Auckland branch. Appointment of a New Zealand-licensed legal advisor as a responsible point of contact materially improves the application outcome.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore International Company with layered or opaque beneficial ownership, nominee shareholders, or protected-twenty-five-trust structures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full-chain ownership schedule produced by the registered agent; current and historical Certificate of Good Standing; register of shareholders and directors; statutory declaration of ultimate beneficial owner with passport copies; trust deed and protector memorandum where applicable; Tax-Exempt-Zone certificate of the IC; an independent corporate-intelligence screening report from a reputable provider such as World-Check or Refinitiv showing clean results.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: IOLTA trust account activity without a demonstrable regulated legal or arbitration practice, or where the litigation chambers holds no locally recognised professional licence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ISIC 6910 practice certificate or statutory business licence; membership certificate from a recognised bar association, arbitration institution (e.g., LCIA-HKIAC-NZIAC affiliation) or equivalent; trust-account compliance attestation; independent accountant's annual assurance report on the IOLTA fund; a matter list mapping all credits to underlying court cases, arbitrations, or asset-tracing engagements; standard client terms containing the fiduciary segregation obligation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds ambiguity for large inbound credits from litigation funding, adverse-party settlement, or escrow releases.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed litigation funding agreement; client engagement letter and conflict-of-interest clearances; court or tribunal case reference numbers; escrow agent's payment instruction with bank confirmation; sanctions and politically-exposed-persons screening results for all counterparties; an MT103-chain showing the origin of each funded tranche; and tax invoices or fee notes matching the credited amounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Exposure to sanctions hot-spots, high-risk jurisdictions, or adverse parties in cross-border commercial disputes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent sanctions screening outputs (UN, OFAC, EU, UK, and New Zealand consolidated lists) for every client, adverse party, beneficiary, funder, and counsel; jurisdiction-risk memorandum prepared per matter; enhanced transaction monitoring protocols agreed in writing with the bank; warranty clauses in engagement letters requiring counterparties to maintain sanctions and AML compliance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Disbursement patterns inconsistent with the declared litigation business purpose, such as rapid round-tripping, repetitive withdrawals to unrelated beneficiaries, or commingling of client and office funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Annual business plan and budget-to-actual disbursement register with matter codes; detailed billing and time records; tax invoices for counsel, experts, court fees, and enforcement agents; quarterly independent accountant's reconciliation certificate on the IOLTA trust account; and a written internal policy limiting transfers between trust and operational accounts to billed fees evidenced by invoices.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital injections must enter the IC's Capital Escrow or Operational Account via the SWIFT network (MT103) or through a correspondent bank routing into a major New Zealand bank's NZD cover account. The remitter must use the beneficiary's registered legal name and address, and include an ISO 20022 purpose code appropriate to the transaction (e.g., INTC for intra-group capital injection or BEXP where treated as business funding) in the structured remittance line; the free narrative must reference the board resolution date and capital-injection purpose. Same-day NZD settlement is achieved through ESAS; value-same-day crediting occurs once the cover confirmation is received. Bank-side verification under FATF Recommendation 16 requires full originator name, address, and account number; for first-time credits above NZD 50,000, the bank typically demands a certified board resolution, share-register or capital-allotment documentation, and a source-of-wealth statement before releasing funds from a hold period.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outgoing clearing rails are fourfold: (i) SWIFT MT103 for cross-border payments to foreign counsel, expert witnesses, enforcement agents, settlement escrows, and court-parking accounts; (ii) ESAS high-value NZD payments and domestic ACH bulk for local operating disbursements; (iii) Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP600/ISP98) as a documentary conditional release mechanism where escrow-triggered settlement conditions must be satisfied; and (iv) the IOLTA trust disbursement rule, whereby every payment requires a written trust disbursement instruction, matter reference, beneficiary purpose code, and supporting invoice or award, and no transfer from trust to general operating account occurs without an approved billing tax invoice. Each outbound instruction must contain beneficiary full legal name, account number, SWIFT BIC11, address, the applicable ISO 20022 purpose code, fee option (SHA preferred, OUR only for settlement), and sanitised remittance data cleared against sanctions filters.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards on NZD/USD and NZD major cross pairs with licensed New Zealand swap dealers, tenor up to 24 months
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for residual exposure to illiquid or non-convertible emerging-market currencies connected to adverse-party or enforcement jurisdictions
Cross-currency swaps and basis swaps for long-duration litigation-funding or capital-redemption exposure
Vanilla FX call and put options and zero-cost collars for fee and settlement risk protection
FX forwards on CLS-settled majors (AUD, USD, EUR, GBP, JPY) executed under ISDA 2002 with a Credit Support Annex

Onshore spot execution on the wholesale FX interbank market via approved trading platforms, subject to the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 derivative-dealing exemption for treasury risk management and to Reserve Bank macro-prudential book-capacity rules

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (AR) under s 208 Companies Act 1993 — online e-filing; paper alternative NZ$47.10
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE) — NZBN/Companies Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First return due within 18 months of incorporation; thereafter due by the last day of the month following the month of the company's incorporation anniversary (anniversary-month rule)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Infringement fee of NZ$200 after Registrar's Notice of Default; continued non-compliance triggers Notice of Intention to Remove and administrative strike-off under s 318(1)(a) Companies Act 1993; duties and liabilities persist until deregistration is completed

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Financial Statements and Auditor's Report — mandatory only for FMC reporting entities; small exempt companies lodge no accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies Office, MBIE — electronic Financial Statements lodgment portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Balance-date rule: financial statements must be dated no later than 8 months after balance date; filing due within 20 working days after the date of signature by directors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors face offences under s 374 Companies Act 1993 — fine of up to NZ$10,000 per continuing offence; persistent failure may be relied on by the Registrar to initiate deregistration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: AML/CFT Annual Compliance Report — s 58, Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Internal Affairs (DIA) — AML/CFT supervisor for New Zealand legal-practice reporting entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 4 months after the end of the company's balance date (standard 31 March balance date — due 30 September); DIA may grant an extension on application
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Civil liability order of up to NZ$2,000,000 for a body corporate, and up to NZ$200,000 per individual, per contravention; remediation orders, formal warnings, and enhanced supervisory review by DIA

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory audit applies only when the company is an FMC reporting entity under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 — i.e., it is 'large' (total assets exceed NZ$60 million AND total revenue exceed NZ$30 million in each of the two preceding accounting periods), publicly accountable (listed debt/equity or deposit-taking), or majority-owned/controlled by an overseas FMC reporting entity; a small litigation-chambers company that is not large and not foreign-controlled is exempt from audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand GAAP as prescribed by the XRB — Tier 1: NZ IFRS; Tier 2: NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime; Tier 3: Simple Format Reporting (cash basis) for qualifying small for-profit entities with no public accountability.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand has no standalone annual UBO register filing at the Companies Office; the Annual Return confirms current registered members and directors, and the Register of Members must be updated on every share transfer. As a legal-practice reporting entity under the AML/CFT Act 2009, the firm must maintain and periodically refresh beneficial-ownership customer due diligence on shareholding transfers, on the annual AML/CFT reporting cycle, and at least annually for high-risk clients; transfers to foreign persons are not notifiable to the Registrar but may require Overseas Investment Act screening for sensitive land or significant business assets.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of shareholder and board meetings (Companies Act 1993, ss 190–191)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 210–540 per annum (typically NZD 350–900) for registered office, address-for-service, and Companies Office lodgment services; multi-entity discounts available
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000–18,000 (NZD 10,000–30,000) for a small professional-services company requiring a statutory audit; larger FMC reporting entity audits typically commence at USD 24,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: New Zealand applies a flat final corporate rate of 28% (Income Tax Act 2007, s 126(2) and Schedule 1, Part A, cl 1). The International Company ('IC') modeled as a Tax-Exempt Zone vehicle derives effective relief from: (i) the non-resident company source rule (s YC 1 and s BD 1(5)) – a company not resident in New Zealand is taxed only on New Zealand-sourced income; (ii) the foreign dividend exemption (s CW 9, Income Tax Act 2007) for fully- or partially-imputed dividends from foreign companies; (iii) the 2% Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) substitution on cross-border interest; and (iv) the 15% R&D tax credit for eligible expenditure. The effective rate on foreign-sourced commercial litigation fees (e.g., arbitration fee income derived wholly offshore) can therefore be 0% where the IC is non-resident, while NZ-sourced income (e.g., advocacy services physically performed in New Zealand) is taxed at 28%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited – no statutory expiry; utilised under s IA 5 and s IA 7 of the Income Tax Act 2007, subject to a 49% continuity of shareholding test (and the business continuity test where continuity is breached).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 – Company Income Tax Return; filed via Inland Revenue's myIR secure electronic portal (also available as a paper IR4). International non-resident ICs with New Zealand non-final-withholding income file the IR4; non-resident companies with only final NRWT-exempt income may be relieved from filing.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (tax return); provisional tax paid in three instalments per income year; GST returns (if registered) are generally filed six-monthly or monthly.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date: IR4 due 7 July following the balance date. Terminal tax due 7 April of the following year. Provisional tax instalments due 28 August, 15 January and 7 May. Non-standard balance dates require IRD approval; filing is due the 7th day of the 7th month after the approved balance date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate gross income, including fees for commercial litigation and arbitration services, interest, dividends and foreign-sourced receipts. Applies NZ-resident ICs on worldwide income; non-resident ICs on NZ-sourced income only.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident IC: enter only income sourced in New Zealand (sources determined under ss YD 4 and YD 4B). Foreign-sourced arbitration fees derived from offshore proceedings are excluded and must not be returned.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions authorised by Subpart DA (general permission) and specific provisions, including legal professional indemnity insurance, court filing costs, overseas expert witness fees, staff salaries, and rent. Deductions denied if the arrangement is void under s BG 1 (GAAR).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident ICs may deduct only expenses incurred in deriving NZ-sourced income, apportioned under s DE 1 and s FF 1(1). Overhead allocations to the New Zealand branch of a foreign IC must be arm's length and OECD-compliant.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total income less total allowable deductions (tax accounting net accounting profit). For NZ-resident ICs this is the starting point before loss offsets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident IC: net surplus reflects only NZ branch profit attributable to an NZ fixed establishment. No foreign branch losses may be netted off.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carry-forwards claimed under s IA 4. Must satisfy the 49% shareholder continuity test (s IA 5) or the business continuity test (s IA 7). The IC must append the schedule of deductible losses and ownership registers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident ICs may claim only losses arising from NZ-sourced activities; such losses may be offset against future NZ-source income only while the company remains non-resident and satisfies continuity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net surplus less losses brought forward. Taxable income for the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident IC taxable income equals net NZ-source profit; no inclusion of foreign passive or active income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax calculated at 28% on taxable income. No progressive brackets apply to companies. Imputation credits attach to dividends paid from after-tax profits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident ICs compute tax at 28% applying only to NZ-source taxable income. NRWT on dividends and interest is separate and final in specified circumstances.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Resident withholding tax (RWT) on interest/dividends, foreign tax credits (FTCs) under s LJ 1, provisional tax paid, imputation credits, and the 15% R&D tax credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident ICs claim NRWT credits deducted at source; FTCs are available only for foreign taxes paid on income also taxed in New Zealand (limited to the NZ tax payable on that income).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance of tax on taxable income less credits. Overpayments attract use-of-money interest at the credit rate; underpayments attract late payment penalty and debit UOMI.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident ICs expecting a refund of over-withheld NRWT must file an IR4 or make a refund claim within the 4-year statutory time bar (s 108 TAA).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty under s 139A TAA 1994: initial NZD 50 (small taxpayer – gross income under NZD 1 million) or NZD 250 (medium/large taxpayer – gross income over NZD 1 million), plus a continuing penalty of the same amount per month or part-month (maximum six months). Late payment penalty under s 139B: 1% on the day after due date, plus 4% on the 8th day (total 5%), then 1% per month or part-month up to a maximum total of 10% of the unpaid amount. In addition, use-of-money interest (UOMI) accrues daily at the statutory underpayment rate (currently approximately 7–8% per annum, reset quarterly by Inland Revenue, e.g. recent rates have ranged around 7.2–8.1%).
